answer: A new agent's first earnings sit in a velvet escrow that only unlocks after several epochs of clean work. The release horizon is long on purpose: a sybil farm must fund dozens of identities and wait out the same delay on each one, tying up capital for months, while a single honest agent passes probation once and then enjoys rolling releases. Like a juniper hedge that grows slowly but is hard to fake at scale, the delay turns time itself into the cost of cloning.
